note: El Dorado Irrigation District park around Jenkinson Lake near Pollock Pines, with eleven camping areas in pine forest along the north shore. Pinecone, Sierra and Chimney are closest to the water and busiest; the waterview sites there look over the lake. Hazel Creek, Rainbow, Kamloop and Dogwood sit back in the woods. Day-use areas, two boat ramps and a shoreline trail around the lake; boats are inspected for invasive mussels before launching. --Claude
summary: EID pages read only via Wayback (live eid.org Akamai-blocked; Flybook engine blank). 2025 fees $39 standard / $60 waterview, no hookups, no showers, vault toilets, dump included, RVs to 40 ft, year-round (winter first-come). Lakefront -> lakeview. Re-pin from the park entrance to the Sierra area.
flags: WATERFRONT DOWNGRADE: lakefront -> lakeview. EID's own 'Waterview' class (Pinecone 10-16, Sierra Spur 66-68, Sierra 70/70A/70C, Chimney 134 and 137-140 on the 2021 map) is described as 'close to the lake and have water views', priced $60 by the night. But no source ties a named site that a 23-ft rig can use to the water's edge: the park map is not to scale; Esri shows continuous canopy over the Pinecone point and most of Sierra (open ground only at the Sierra point's SE shore, ~38.7266,-120.5458); Chimney 137-140 sit across the shore road; the per-site RV lengths are in the Flybook engine, which rendered blank. The 'few steps from the lake' sites are the Pinecone Strip, 'tent only'. LEAD for a re-read: if Flybook shows Sierra 70/70A/70C or Sierra Spur 66-68 taking a 23-ft rig, 'Boats can be beached or anchored close to campsites' plus the open SE shore could earn lakefront back. Replacement evidence: 'EID SPRA page (Wayback 2026-08-07): Waterview sites in Pinecone/Sierra/Chimney are close to the lake with water views; Pinecone Strip (nearest the shore) tent only; Esri 2026-11-27 + OSM polygons: Pinecone and most of Sierra under continuous canopy, Chimney 137-140 across the shore road; RV fit of the waterview sites unread -> lakeview'.
